newsitem.title: ITALY: Homeless immigrants occupy church in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Homeless immigrants occupy church in Milan.

text.p: Some 60 homeless immigrants occupied a church in central Milan on Wednesday to protest over their removal by local authorities from a hostel they had been using for five years.
All the immigrants, many of them from North Africa, have residence permits and jobs, but are not entitled to live permanently in Italy.
"We want a home. Five of us began a hunger strike five days ago. We will not go away without a roof" one of the immigrants told Reuters inside the church of San Bernardino alle Ossa.
The immigrants were evicted from their hostel last week after ignoring repeated orders to leave.
"We know that it will be impossible to be given accommodation in a few days, but we insist that we will not go away without a home" another immigrant said.
An occupation by illegal immigrants of a church in Paris over the summer drew international attention. Police were sent in to eject the immigrants who were forcibly repatriated.

"We need a solution because the situation could become very dangerous" Virginio Colmegna, a director of Catholic charity Caritas, said. "This is not the same situation as in Paris, these are not people without (work) permits, but we can't give them hospitality in the church," he added.
A delegation of immigrants was due to meet the city councillor responsible for social services, Mariagrazie Dente, later on Wednesday.
"A lot of Italian people are without a home and they don't occupy churches" Dente told Reuters.
